title: Can the opening of a door be an angle?
description: A door fixed to a wall can be open a little or a lot. The place where the door turns, and the two lines that make the opening, are found, to see whether the opening is an angle with a vertex and two arms.
teaching_notes: One idea: the opening of a door is an angle whose vertex is where the door meets the wall and whose arms are the edge of the door and the wall. Watch for students who take the floor or the doorway as an arm.

source: Figure it Out: Where are the angles?, Q2
video_script.why: The child finds the vertex and the two arms of an angle in a real door, as the solved example did for the clock hands.
video_script.substitution: A door fixed to a wall, opened by different amounts.
video_script.anchor: a door fixed to a wall, drawn from above with the door open by different amounts
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the amount a door is open is an angle

final_answer.value: Yes; the vertex is the point where the door meets the wall (the hinge); the arms are the edge of the door and the wall
final_answer.spoken: the vertex is the point where the door meets the wall

maths_rules: an angle has two arms that meet at a vertex
the vertex of the door angle is the point where the door meets the wall, the hinge
the arms are the edge of the door and the wall
a closed door lies on the wall, so its arms lie on each other and the opening is zero
video_script.design: A door seen from above stays on the board and opens by steps. The vertex and the two arms light up one at a time, and the word hinge is held back until the answer line.
